Interpretation: At the α = 0.05 significance level, there is statistically significant evidence to reject the null hypothesis (t(156.0) = 12.53, p < 0.001, one-tailed). Winning teams achieved a significantly higher average pass-completion (M = 85.15%, SD = 2.83%) than losing teams (M = 79.20%, SD = 3.13%), with a mean difference of 5.95 (95% CI [5.02, 6.89]). The standardized effect size is Cohen's d = 1.99, indicating a large practical effect of passing accuracy on match success.
